title: NeoMME compresses visual document retrieval into one smaller encoder
friendlyTitle: A smaller open model searches text and document images together
summary: H Company released Apache-2.0 NeoMME models with 260 million and 800 million parameters for multilingual text and image encoding. A single bidirectional Transformer handles both modalities; the team reports about 51 document pages per second for the smaller model on an NVIDIA L40S and a 255-fold reduction in one retrieval-index format while retaining more than 95% of baseline quality.
friendlySummary: NeoMME uses one AI encoder for words and page images. Its makers report fast document processing and much smaller search indexes, and they released the models openly.
whyItMatters: Smaller visual retrievers can make search over scanned forms, reports and mixed-layout documents cheaper to operate. The open checkpoints and Transformers support make the claims testable, but teams should benchmark accuracy and storage on their own languages and document types.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This could lower the cost of searching scanned documents and complex reports. Try it with your own languages and page layouts before depending on it.
